--- title: "Cross-sectional analysis" date: 07/25/2023 author: Reinout Schols categories: [Factor analysis, item analysis, multiple regression analysis, R] include: true editor: visual warning: false message: false format: html: code-fold: true code-tools: true highlight-style: github --- **In this post, I will explain my reasoning and results of a factor and item analysis followed up by a multiple regression analysis.** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Context: - 134 participants from the Netherlands with an age between 16 and 40 years old. - Measured on one moment. - based on the reasoned action approach theory (the intention to perform behavior is determined by attitude, perceived norm and perceived behavioral control.) Research question: ::: {.callout-important icon="false"} *What are the most important determinants from the reasoned action approach in influencing wearing earplugs or not during leisure activities .* ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #| include: false library(readr) library(rosetta) library(haven) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(tidyverse) library(behaviorchange) library(psych) library(corrplot) library(car) library(EFAtools) library(papaja) library(rempsyc) library(readr) library(rosetta) library(haven) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(tidyverse) library(behaviorchange) library(psych) library(corrplot) library(car) library(EFAtools) library(papaja) library(rempsyc) ``` ::: # factor analysis{style="color:LightSteelBlue"} ## checking assumptions factor analysis {style="color:white"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # create correlation table of data res <- cor(Clean_data_16_40_assump1) # Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin criterion (KMO) KMO(res) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ── Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin criterion (KMO) ────────────────────────────────────────── ✔ The overall KMO value for your data is middling. These data are probably suitable for factor analysis. Overall: 0.705 For each variable: epw_AttDirect_good epw_AttDirect_pleas 0.652 0.672 epw_AttDirect_smart epw_AttDirect_healt 0.590 0.546 epw_AttDirect_excit epw_PBCDirect_ifwanted 0.341 0.771 epw_PBCDirect_easy epw_PBCDirect_control 0.745 0.712 epw_PBCDirect_externalFactors epw_PBCDirect_notOnlyMe 0.769 0.708 epw_NrmDirect_in1 epw_NrmDirect_in2 0.758 0.752 epw_NrmDirect_dn1 epw_NrmDirect_dn2 0.723 0.774 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important icon="false"} - An overall KMO value of 0.705, which means the data is relatively suited for a factor analysis. ::: ## Performing factor analysis {style="color:LightSteelBlue"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 3 factors and three determinants rosetta::factorAnalysis( data = Clean_data_16_40, nfactors = 3, items = relevante_variabelen_1, fm = "minres", rotate = "oblimin", screePlot = TRUE, correlations = TRUE, summary = TRUE ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ```{.r .cell-code} #Zelf screeplot maken van factor analyses n <- dim(res)[1] scree_tb <- tibble(x = 1:n, y = sort(eigen(res)$value, decreasing = TRUE)) scree_plot <- scree_tb |> ggplot(aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:n) + ggtitle("Scree plot") + labs(x = "# factors", y = "Eigenvalue") scree_plot ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](cross-sec_index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important icon="false"} - Based on the theory the data was forced onto three factors. Three items don't load properly on the factors : - epw_PBCDirect_externalFactors - epw_AttDirect_pleas - epw_AttDirect_excit ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #| include: false # Aggregating validated items #Intentie Clean_data_16_40$Intentie <- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40, "epw_Intention_plan", "epw_Intention_will", "epw_Intention_want" ); # directe attitude Clean_data_16_40$Attitude_Agg <- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40, "epw_AttDirect_smart", "epw_AttDirect_healt" ); # Directe normen Clean_data_16_40$Norm_Agg<- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40, "epw_NrmDirect_in1", "epw_NrmDirect_in2", "epw_NrmDirect_dn1", "epw_NrmDirect_dn2" ); # directe gedragscontrole Clean_data_16_40$Gedragscontrole_Agg <- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40, "epw_PBCDirect_ifwanted", "epw_PBCDirect_easy", "epw_PBCDirect_control", "epw_PBCDirect_notOnlyMe" ); #Intentie Clean_data_16_40_assump$Intentie <- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40_assump, "epw_Intention_plan", "epw_Intention_will", "epw_Intention_want" ); # directe attitude Clean_data_16_40_assump$Attitude_Agg <- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40_assump, "epw_AttDirect_smart", "epw_AttDirect_healt" ); # Directe normen Clean_data_16_40_assump$Norm_Agg<- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40_assump, "epw_NrmDirect_in1", "epw_NrmDirect_in2", "epw_NrmDirect_dn1", "epw_NrmDirect_dn2" ); # directe gedragscontrole Clean_data_16_40_assump$Gedragscontrole_Agg <- rosetta::means( data = Clean_data_16_40_assump, "epw_PBCDirect_ifwanted", "epw_PBCDirect_easy", "epw_PBCDirect_control", "epw_PBCDirect_notOnlyMe" ); ``` ::: # Ciber plots {style="color:white"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ciber plots alle drie de determinanten behaviorchange::CIBER(data=Clean_data_16_40, determinants=c( "epw_PBCDirect_ifwanted", "epw_PBCDirect_easy", "epw_PBCDirect_control", "epw_PBCDirect_notOnlyMe", "epw_PBCDirect_externalFactors_RECODED", "Gedragscontrole_Agg", "epw_NrmDirect_in1", "epw_NrmDirect_in2", "epw_NrmDirect_dn1", "epw_NrmDirect_dn2", "Norm_Agg", "epw_AttDirect_good", "epw_AttDirect_pleas", "epw_AttDirect_smart", "epw_AttDirect_healt", "epw_AttDirect_excit", "Attitude_Agg"),targets=c( 'epw_intention')) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](cross-sec_index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important icon="false"} - Ciber plots give an overview of all seperate items and the importance of each item on the dependent variable. ::: # Multiple reggression analysis {style="color:white"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rosetta::regr( Intentie ~ Attitude_Agg+ Gedragscontrole_Agg + Norm_Agg, collinearity = TRUE, data=Clean_data_16_40 ); ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
::: {.cell} ::: ### Regression analysis {#rosettaRegr-Jm3CuE4c8L} **Summary** ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](cross-sec_index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(Clean_data_16_40, aes(Intentie, Attitude_Agg)) + geom_point() + theme_apa() + stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, geom = "smooth", color = "black") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](cross-sec_index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(Clean_data_16_40, aes(Intentie, Gedragscontrole_Agg)) + geom_point() + theme_apa() + stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, geom = "smooth", color = "black") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](cross-sec_index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-2.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(Clean_data_16_40, aes(Intentie, Norm_Agg)) + geom_point() + theme_apa() + stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, geom = "smooth", color = "black") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](cross-sec_index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-3.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important icon="false"} assumpties uitleggen ::: **Conclusion of multiple regression analysis:** ::: {.callout-important icon="false"} - Both interventions (medication and therapy) have a significant effect on psychological wellbeing. - Therapy had a stronger influence than medication. - See [github](https://github.com/ReinoutSchols/code-longitudinal-course.git) for full analysis :::
